annotations.text:
HOW TO READ THIS

Five directions, same placeholder content in each, only the style changes. Square brackets are facts to fill in later. Mission text is a draft to react to, not final.

Mix and match freely: e.g. Paper's typography with Botanical's daisy, or Index's fact table on any of them.

Bottom row: six wordmark treatments, independent of the direction.

PAPER (leading candidate)

Why: closest to the CAISH feel you liked. Serif headlines, monospace labels, warm paper, one accent (Dartmouth green on a single italic phrase). One narrow column, everything on the page, nothing hidden.

Tradeoff: quiet. Relies entirely on copy and type; there is no image to catch the eye in the first five seconds.

GREEN FIELD

Why: owns Dartmouth green loudly. Big statement hero, one obvious button, bordered cards. Looks like an established org from day one, closest to the Columbia / Oxford sites.

Tradeoff: least minimal of the five. Can read as a department page rather than a student group, and a solid green block is a big commitment.

ESSAY

Why: the LessWrong lineage. Serif body, sans headings, green links, a table of contents instead of a marketing layout. The whole site is one well-typeset document, which is the most honest form of 'nothing hidden'.

Tradeoff: text-heavy and looks like a post more than an organization. No visual hook; people who skim will bounce.

BOTANICAL

Why: owns the name. A line-drawn daisy is the 'eye-catching image' Kairos asks for without needing photos. Warmer type, rounded cards, softer tone, which directly lowers the 'this is a scary commitment' feeling.

Tradeoff: can read as cute or unserious to exactly the technical students you most want. Easy to overdo.

INDEX

Why: 'nothing hidden' taken literally. The site is a well-set table of facts: Swiss grid, hairlines, monospace metadata, a key-value block in the hero that answers every practical question at once. Unlike any other group site.

Tradeoff: cold. Least welcoming for non-technical students, and every new section needs a new row.

WORDMARKS

Six treatments of the name. A to C are type only; D to F add a daisy mark. C (italic lowercase green) and D (line daisy) are my picks. The full official name only ever appears in small footer text.
